## Q1
What is the difference between the average semester fees of BCA and average semester fees of MCA during 2016-2020?

Study the table of semester fees for four courses during 2016-2020.

| Year | BCA | MCA | MTech | MPhil |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | 25,000 | 52,000 | 60,200 | 30,000 |
| 2017 | 26,500 | 53,500 | 61,400 | 32,000 |
| 2018 | 27,200 | 54,200 | 62,500 | 32,600 |
| 2019 | 27,600 | 55,700 | 62,900 | 33,400 |
| 2020 | 28,000 | 56,800 | 63,700 | 33,900 |

## Q1 - Options
(A) 27,200
(B) 27,365
(C) 27,580
(D) 27,400

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Data Interpretation
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q1

BCA totals 134,300, so its average is 26,860. MCA totals 272,200, so its average is 54,440. The difference is 54,440 - 26,860 = 27,580.

## Q8
Given below are two statements.<br>
Statement I: The ability to form and use symbols (words, gestures, signs, images, and so on) is accomplished in the preoperational period.<br>
Statement II: According to Piaget, preoperational children do not have a tendency to be egocentric. In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.

## Q8 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
(C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
(D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Teaching Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q8

Piaget associates symbolic thought with the preoperational stage, so Statement I is true. Preoperational children are characteristically egocentric, so Statement II is false.

## Q11
If a researcher has to test a hypothesis whether the difference between the means of two groups is significant, she/he will use:

## Q11 - Options
(A) Chi-square test
(B) Correlation coefficient
(C) Sign-test
(D) Student's t-test

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q11

Student's t-test compares the means of two groups when testing whether their difference is statistically significant. Chi-square tests categorical association instead.

## Q12
Which of the following are the stages of meta analysis?<br>
A. Understand the literature<br>
B. Conduct new studies to fill the gap<br>
C. Develop inclusion and exclusion criteria of the study<br>
D. Locating primary studies<br>
E. Identify secondary data Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

## Q12 - Options
(A) A, B and D only
(B) B, C and D only
(C) A, C and D only
(D) B, D and E only

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q12

Meta-analysis begins by understanding the literature, setting inclusion and exclusion criteria, and locating primary studies. Conducting new studies is not a stage of synthesising existing studies.

## Q13 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Research Aptitude
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q13

Parametric tests can be more powerful when their assumptions hold. They are not assumption-free because they rely on conditions such as distributional form and scale.

## Q23
The ages of Swati and Manisha are in the ratio of 5:6 and the sum of their ages is 55 years. What will be the ratio of their ages after 5 years?

## Q23 - Options
(A) 6:7
(B) 7:6
(C) 6:5
(D) 5:6

## Q23 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q23

The present ages are 25 and 30 because 5x + 6x = 55. After five years they are 30 and 35, which reduces to 6:7.

## Q24
Given below are two statements.<br>
Statement I: A vehicle's speed of 30.6 km/hr is the same as 5.8 m/s.<br>
Statement II: The speed of a bus is 72 km/hr. The distance covered by the bus in 10 seconds is 100 metre. In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

## Q24 - Options
(A) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(B) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(C) Statement I is true but Statement II is false
(D) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

## Q24 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Mathematical Aptitude (Arithmetic)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q24

30.6 km/h equals 30.6 × 5/18 = 8.5 m/s, not 5.8 m/s. Also 72 km/h is 20 m/s, so in 10 seconds the bus covers 200 m, not 100 m.

## Q25 - Hint

## Q26
Which of the following statements correctly apply to deductive arguments?<br>
A. Deductive arguments are either valid or invalid.<br>
B. There must be a necessary relation between the premises and the conclusion.<br>
C. Adding new premises improves the validity.<br>
D. False premises may lead to a true conclusion. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

## Q26 - Options
(A) A, B and C only
(B) A, B and D only
(C) A, C and D only
(D) B, C and D only

## Q26 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q26

Deductive arguments are assessed as valid or invalid, and validity concerns a necessary link from premises to conclusion. False premises can still yield a true conclusion. Adding premises does not itself improve validity.

## Q27
Identify the fallacy committed in the argument: Since no tragic actors are idiots and some comedians are not idiots, so some comedians are not tragic actors.

## Q27 - Options
(A) Fallacy of the Illicit Process of Major Term
(B) Fallacy of the Illicit Process of Minor Term
(C) Existential Fallacy
(D) Fallacy of Exclusive Premises

## Q27 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q27

The premises distribute neither term in the way needed to infer a relation between comedians and tragic actors. The conclusion improperly combines two negative premises, an exclusive-premises fallacy.

## Q28

## Q28 - Options
(A) Appeal to ignorance
(B) Straw man
(C) Appeal to unqualified authority
(D) Red herring

## Q28 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Logical Reasoning (Venn, Syllogism, Arguments)
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q28

The argument treats failure to prove a claim as proof that the claim is false. That is an appeal to ignorance.

## Q46
What is the focus of this text?

Assessment is central to almost all forms of education around the world, and in recent years, a wider variety of assessment has tended to be used. One such form is peer and self-assessment. Self-assessment is the ability to critically assess one's own work. Peer assessment is making judgments about, or commenting upon, each other's work. Both have strengths and weaknesses. With careful initiation and moderation, they can be effective. However, the author argues that in the high-stakes environments of most educational settings, these methods are inappropriate because marking is unreliable.

Peer and self-assessment have become increasingly common, particularly in further and higher education. They can reduce teachers' marking loads and enhance group work and students' critical-thinking skills. If marking criteria are discussed and agreed at the start, students' marks tend to be similar to teachers' marks. With suitable initial training, work marked by a student may not differ from work marked by a teacher.

(B) Assessment and Education
(C) Assessment in general
(D) Peer and Self-assessment

## Q46 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Comprehension
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q46

The passage discusses both peer assessment and self-assessment, their claimed benefits and their limits. Its focus is therefore peer and self-assessment together.
